question: Does the finite-ratio low-index boundary remain correct for miscalibrated predictions with a free intercept, and is Brier risk alone sufficient at finite auxiliary ratios?
positive_powers: population variance-optimal for an orthogonal slope, clipped to[0,1]; established covariance formula
identity_checks: asymmetric prediction does not force zero intercept multiplier
matched_moment_proposition: A balanced-null analytical counterexample will compare frozen confidence distributions with equal prediction mean, Brier risk and all fixed-power orthogonal-score covariances. It is deterministic mathematical illustration, not outcome-selected simulation evidence.
retain: all feasibility, exterior, unresolved statuses; all simulation conditions; no adaptive stopping
scope: fixed low-index predictors and fixed powers; no learned-predictor or data-selected-power phase theorem
